propositions: On a 30 GiB root volume, the snapshot janitor's absolute 2 GiB free watermark is only crossed at 93.3% used, above the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% peak reached during the incident, making the reclaim trigger structurally unreachable.

Every review materializes a fresh ~620 MiB copy of the 69,984-file ticket tree on a content-addressed key that advances every ~26 seconds with single-file deltas, producing ~0.85 GiB per review and 4.4 GiB/h disk growth.

The snapshot store lives on the container writable layer (root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere, so store_root() falls through to tempfile.gettempdir() instead of a separate volume.

The 90% → 48% drop and all 23 reclaim events are container recreations destroying the ephemeral writable layer wholesale, not variable-residue Docker prune operations, proven by convergence on an identical 48% floor.

Adding a volume-relative headroom term (free_watermark_pct as whole percent of total volume) with hysteresis allows the janitor to reclaim before 85% alarm floor on small volumes while remaining unchanged when the knob defaults to 0.

The 7-day cold-trim trigger is dead code on a container with hours-long lifetime across 23 recreations in 4 days, and the ADR-promised byte-total backstop is absent from _gc_pass and never called by materialize_tickets.
